newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo precious metal futures end mixed.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo precious metal futures end mixed.

text.p: Tokyo precious metal futures closed mixed on Friday, as local investors were sidelined due to Japan's "Golden Week" holidays, traders said. The market will be closed next Monday for a national holiday.

Yen-based gold futures ended three yen lower to six yen higher, with the benchmark April 1998 contract down one yen at 1,383 yen per gram. Spot gold was quoted at $340.20/50 per ounce at 0730 GMT, against $340.15/65 in New York on Thursday.
Light technical orders from local investors dominated trading today, traders said. "Players will return to the market next Tuesday," a brokerage house trader said.
Yen-based platinum futures ended steady to lower, with the benchmark April 1998 contract down four yen at 1,476 yen per gram.
Palladium futures were mixed, with prices ranging from two yen lower to six yen higher. Benchmark April was up one yen at 607 yen per gram.

The platinum group metal market will remain nervous until the long-delayed Russia-Japan export talks for this year are set, traders said. "We welcome any news about the talks," an analyst at a brokerage house said.
Silver futures were higher in all months, with benchmark April up 1.8 yen at 195.9 yen per 10 grams.
